tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Sentence Structure & Translation

questions.question: Q: What is the typical word order of a Latin sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: Subject-Object-Verb (SOV). The verb usually comes at or near the end. However, word order is flexible because case endings show grammatical relationships.

questions.question: Q: What does GNC agreement mean for adjectives?
questions.correctAnswer: Gender, Number, Case: an adjective must match the noun it describes in all three. For example, puella bona (fem. nom. sg.) but servum bonum (masc. acc. sg.).

questions.question: Q: How does the relative pronoun agree with its antecedent?
questions.correctAnswer: The relative pronoun agrees with its antecedent in gender and number, but its case is determined by its function within the relative clause itself.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on Sentence Structure & Translation

questions.question: Q: What is the accusative + infinitive construction?
questions.correctAnswer: Indirect statement: the subject of reported speech is in the accusative, and the verb becomes an infinitive. Example: dicit puellam venire (he says the girl is coming).

questions.question: Q: How do you distinguish a purpose clause from a result clause?
questions.correctAnswer: Both use ut + subjunctive, but a purpose clause translates as 'in order to' and has no signal word in the main clause. A result clause translates as 'so...that' and is signalled by tam, tantus, ita, or similar in the main clause.

questions.question: Q: What does cum + subjunctive mean and how does context change its translation?
questions.correctAnswer: Cum can mean 'when' (temporal), 'since' (causal), or 'although' (concessive), depending on context. All three use the subjunctive mood.

questions.question: Q: How do you translate ne + subjunctive?
questions.correctAnswer: Ne + subjunctive forms a negative purpose clause ('in order not to') or a negative indirect command ('not to'). Example: venit ne pater videret (he came so that his father would not see).

questions.question: Q: What is the enclitic -que and how does it differ from et?
questions.correctAnswer: -que means 'and' but is attached to the end of the second word (puellae puerique — girls and boys), whereas et stands as a separate word. -que is more emphatic, joining the pair closely.
